Add a cover What you're doing: giving the book its face. A cover in Beuk is a real part of the EPUB — declared properly, shown first, and recognised by every store's catalogue. Steps Open Project Settings and find the Cover Image block. Upload a JPG or PNG . For store catalogues, bigger is better: Kindle recommends 2560 × 1600 px. A small image uploads fine but may be refused by a store later. The cover appears at the head of Front Matter. Select it there to see it on the device canvas. Export as usual. The EPUB now carries the image, a cover page first in the reading order, and a cover landmark in the navigation — the thing screen readers and store ingesters look for. Changed your mind? Remove in Project Settings and the package returns to exactly its coverless self — no residue. What can go wrong The store says my cover is too small. That's the store's catalogue rule, not the EPUB's fault. Upload the largest version you have; for print-adjacent sizes, 2560 px on the long side keeps everyone happy. The cover looks stretched. Covers are shown at their own proportions — if the file itself is an odd shape, the preview shows that honestly. Crop in an image editor before uploading. No cover yet — can I export anyway? Yes. Beuk exports a complete, valid book without one; the validator will note it as a friendly warning, never an error.
